title: Parity's failing systems carry every hard instance
claim: Parity's failing systems carry every hard instance of its coupling family. (i) Splice lemma: if a signed cubic piece has a parity certificate, a set s of lines covering every point evenly with b.s = 1, and s avoids a line m, then swapping an incidence (q, m) of the piece with an incidence (p, l) of any host gives a cubic system that is again parity-unsolvable, with the same certificate. (ii) Two calls: with G the piece's 2x2 transfer matrix from the host point's colour to the colour delivered to the host line, and H_k the host with one incidence replaced by a chain of k pieces, M(H_k) = sum over x, y of F(x, y) G^k(x, y), so M(H) = (tr G M(H_1) - M(H_2)) / det G by Cayley-Hamilton. (iii) The eight-line piece from the census (no repeated lines, one negated line) has det G = -16 lam^2 (lam - 1)^6 (lam + 1)^6. So for every complex lam outside {0, 1, -1}, counting parity's coupling on connected simple cubic systems reduces with two oracle calls to counting it on connected simple parity-unsolvable systems, without repeated lines when the host has none; with ticket A it is #P-hard there for every lam outside {0, 1, -1, i, -i, oo}. Parity's failing class makes no member of its family easy. Contrast (observed): splicing a not-all-equal-unsolvable piece into a 2-colourable host gave a 2-colourable system in every tested case, so the knot's failures do not transplant.
failure_conditions: A spliced system that is parity-solvable, not cubic, not simple, disconnected, or has a repeated line when the host has none.
A host and coupling where the two-call formula disagrees with the directly computed count.
A complex lam outside {0, 1, -1} where det G vanishes.
foundation_claim_scope: A reduction between two instance classes of one weighted counting family; no knot, contact or topology claim.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session on 2026-10-31, at the owner's request relayed by a peer session that found the error.
validation.status: checked: the piece's certificate and transfer matrix; structure of every spliced system; the two-call formula end to end on plain and signed hosts at real and complex couplings; the knot contrast on census hosts; no human or external review
validation.novelty: Elementary (certificate-preserving splicing and Cayley-Hamilton interpolation are standard Holant tools); recorded as part of the correction, not as a discovery.
